messages:
maria.su: Heads-up — customer AcmePay reported a huge unexpected invoice after a long streaming generation. Dashboard shows ~1.2M tokens, invoice charged ~1.8M. They use EventSource + client-side cancel/reconnect a few times.
olivia.billing: yikes. do we have the raw metering events or request ids? any sample session id from them? :worried:
sanjay.runtime: can you paste the earliest and latest request_ids or the SSE stream id? I want to check whether the finalization path ran twice (we've seen that before when client sends a second FIN-like event).
maria.su: session id is "sess_8Xz9A" and customer shared logs: they show two server-side `FINAL_CHUNK` entries for the same stream id separated by a short gap. Posting redacted snippet below.
kevin.client: repro steps I used locally:
```
# open EventSource stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-large" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"write long story","stream":true}' | sed -n '1,200p'
# after ~10s send client cancel (SIGINT)
# then immediately reopen a new EventSource for same logical conversation id
```
maria.su: attached customer log excerpt:
```
[2025-11-04T15:21:12.123Z] stream(sess_8Xz9A) -> CHUNK id=42 len=512
[2025-11-04T15:21:16.450Z] stream(sess_8Xz9A) -> FINAL_CHUNK checksum=0x9b7a
[2025-11-04T15:21:16.470Z] client(sess_8Xz9A) -> CANCEL
[2025-11-04T15:21:16.880Z] stream(sess_8Xz9A) -> FINAL_CHUNK checksum=0x9b7a
```
olivia.billing: so two FINALs with same checksum. dashboard token sum counts ~1.2M but invoice prob summed both FINAL contributions. can we determine which event the billing pipeline consumed twice?
billing-bot: metering.event -> saved: {cust:acmepay, stream:sess_8Xz9A, event:FINAL_CHUNK, tokens:1420, id:evt_33421}
billing-bot: metering.event -> saved: {cust:acmepay, stream:sess_8Xz9A, event:FINAL_CHUNK, tokens:1420, id:evt_33422}
sanjay.runtime: thanks. looks like two metering rows for same final checkpoint. probable root cause: race between `finalize_stream()` and a reconnect handler which also triggers finalize if it sees residual KV cache. Both paths call the metering emit before dedupe check.
kevin.client: I can reproduce reliably if I cancel then reopen within ~200-400ms.
maria.su: customer timeline: they canceled then re-opened quickly during an unstable mobile connection.
sanjay.runtime: short-term mitigation: we have a config flag `streaming.dedupe_final=true` you can flip in prod to cause the metering producer to dedupe on (stream_id, checksum). it'll prevent double-write but keep the second event idempotent.
olivia.billing: can we run a one-off SQL to identify affected invoices? something like:
```
SELECT invoice_id, SUM(tokens) as billed_tokens, COUNT(*) as duplicate_final_count
FROM metering.events
WHERE event = 'FINAL_CHUNK' AND stream_id = 'sess_8Xz9A'
GROUP BY invoice_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```
olivia.billing: if we find duplicates across many streams for same customer we'll issue credit.
sanjay.runtime: long-term fix: will add an inline dedupe at emission point and add an at-most-once tokenization anchor using `final_checksum` + `stream_seq`. also adding a 1s debounce window on finalize for reconnect-related flows.
maria.su: steps taken so far:
- enabled `streaming.dedupe_final=true` in staging (passed basic tests)
- ran dedupe job against last 30 days for AcmePay to aggregate duplicates (partial results show ~580k duplicated tokens)
- opened internal bug: RDW-3124
kevin.client: for reproducer I'm attaching a tiny script that does cancel/reopen in a loop (works on mac/linux), want me to share it with eng? :+1:
sanjay.runtime: please do. also include `--wait 250` to hit the window.
kevin.client: pasted gist url: https://gist.github.com/kevin/stream-reopen-repro
maria.su: customer asked for timeline and provisional credit. olivia can you estimate credit amount from current dedupe run?
olivia.billing: provisional credit estimate = duplicated_tokens * avg_token_price. using current pricing that's about ~$1,250. I'll prepare a credit note and route to finance after engineering confirms dedupe job completeness.
deploy-bot: deploy: streaming.dedupe_final=true rolled out to prod-canary at 2025-11-04T16:02:30Z by sanjay.runtime
sanjay.runtime: small note — we need to backfill metering events created between 2025-10-05 and 2025-11-04 for customers with >1 FINAL per stream. I'll run a targeted dedupe/backfill job next 24h and post results.
maria.su: passing to CS: will follow up with customer, propose credit, and offer advice: avoid immediate reopen within 1s as interim workaround. will update thread after backfill.
olivia.billing: thanks — loop me in on the customer reply. :pray:
maria.su: closing loop for now, will reopen if customer sees further discrepant charges.
